title: Square roots of a rational number
competency: Calculate the square root of perfect squares.

keywords.def: If a² = b, then a is a square root of b.
The positive square root of a number, written √b.
The symbol √ (or ∛ for a cube root).
The number under the radical sign: in √b, b is the radicand.

en.text: A square root undoes squaring. If a² = b, then a is a square root of b. 16 has two square roots, 4 and −4; the positive one, √16 = 4, is the principal square root. Negative numbers have no rational square root, and √0 = 0.

am.text: ካሬ ሥር ማካሬን ይቀለብሳል። a² = b ከሆነ a የ b ካሬ ሥር ነው። √16 = 4 ዋናው ካሬ ሥር ነው። አሉታዊ ቁጥሮች ምክንያታዊ ካሬ ሥር የላቸውም።

screens.title: From area to side
screens.ask: A square garden has an area of 16 m². How long is each side?
screens.after: 4 m, because 4 × 4 = 16. Finding the side from the area is taking the square root.

screens.title: 16 squares
screens.intro: These 16 small squares make one big square. Fill it row by row.
say: Four rows of 4 make 16. So the side is 4: √16 = 4.

screens.title: Square roots
paras: Definition 2.3: If a² = b, then a is called a square root of b.
The square root of 4 is 2, because 2² = 4.
The square root of 25/64 is 5/8, because (5/8)² = 25/64.
Extracting a square root is the inverse of squaring.

screens.title: The radical sign
paras: 16 = 4 × 4 = (−4) × (−4). So 4 and −4 are both square roots of 16.
The positive one is the principal square root.
The symbol √ is the radical sign. √16 = 4 and −√16 = −4.
In √b, the number b is called the radicand.
screens.note: Negative numbers have no square root in ℚ. The square root of 0 is 0. In power form, √a = a^(1/2).

defs: If a² = b, then a is a square root of b.

screens.title: Find √(25/100)
steps: The principal square root is the positive one: 5/10.

screens.why:
Ask: which number times itself gives 121?
11 × 11 = 121.
√ always means the positive root, so √121 = 11 (not −11).
60.5 is 121 ÷ 2: halving is not a square root.
screens.clue: Which positive number times itself is 121?

screens.why:
Take the root of the top: √25 = 5 (5 × 5 = 25).
Take the root of the bottom: √64 = 8 (8 × 8 = 64).
So √(25/64) = 5/8.
Check: 5/8 × 5/8 = 25/64. ✓
screens.clue: Take the square root of the top and of the bottom.

screens.text: True or false? √(−9) is a rational number.
screens.why:
A square root of −9 would be a number that times itself gives −9.
positive × positive = positive, and negative × negative = positive.
So no rational number squared can be −9. False.
screens.clue: Can a square ever be negative?

screens.text: How many square roots does 16 have?
screens.why:
4 × 4 = 16.
(−4) × (−4) = 16 too.
So 16 has two square roots, 4 and −4.
The symbol √16 means only the positive one: √16 = 4.

screens.ask: Undo the square root: √x = 0.3. Then x = ___
screens.why:
A square root and a square undo each other.
If √x = 0.3, square both sides: x = (0.3)².
(0.3)² = 0.3 × 0.3: 3 × 3 = 9 with 1 + 1 = 2 decimal places → 0.09.
Check: √0.09 = 0.3, because 0.3 × 0.3 = 0.09. ✓
A common slip is 0.9. But 0.9 × 0.9 = 0.81, so √0.9 is not 0.3.

en.text: To find a square root, write the number as a product of primes with a factor tree, share the primes into two equal groups, and take one group. 400 = (2 × 2 × 5) × (2 × 2 × 5) = 20 × 20, so √400 = 20.

am.text: ካሬ ሥርን ለማግኘት ቁጥሩን በፍጹም ቁጥሮች አባዛ ጻፍ፣ ሁለት እኩል ቡድን አድርግና አንዱን ውሰድ። 400 = 20 × 20፣ ስለዚህ √400 = 20።

screens.title: Two equal groups
screens.ask: 64 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2. Can you share these six 2s into two equal groups?
screens.after: Yes. Each group is 2 × 2 × 2 = 8, and 8 × 8 = 64. So √64 = 8. Watch the tree below.

screens.title: Example 2.11 a: √64 with a factor tree
Using prime factorization
paras: Step 1: grow a factor tree until every leaf is a prime number.
Step 2: share the primes into two equal groups.
Step 3: one group is the square root.
If the primes cannot be shared equally, the number is not a perfect square.

screens.title: Key word again
defs: If a² = b, then a is a square root of b.

screens.title: Example 2.11 c: √400 with a factor tree

screens.why:
Two equal groups: (2 × 5) and (2 × 5).
Each group is 2 × 5 = 10.
100 = 10 × 10, so √100 = 10.

screens.title: Grow the tree for 1225, then type √1225.
screens.clue: Look at the two equal groups. Multiply the numbers in one group.
Count the 2s in 256 and halve them.

screens.why:
576 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 (six 2s and two 3s).
Each group gets three 2s and one 3: 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 = 24.
576 = 24 × 24, so √576 = 24.
screens.clue: Divide by 2 again and again, then by 3.

opts: No: the three 2s cannot be shared equally between two groups
screens.ans: No: the three 2s cannot be shared equally between two groups
screens.why:
For two equal groups, each prime must appear an even number of times.
3 appears twice: fine, one in each group.
2 appears three times: one group would get an extra 2.
So 72 is not a perfect square. (8² = 64 and 9² = 81, and 72 is in between.)
screens.clue: Can each prime be shared equally between two groups?

items.why:
625 = 5 × 125.
125 = 5 × 25.
25 = 5 × 5.
Every factor must be prime, so 625 = 5 × 5 × 5 × 5. (25 and 125 are not prime.)

0 × 0 = 0.
So the square root of 0 is 0.

items.ask: A square has an area of 144 cm². Each side = ___ cm
items.why:
Area = side × side, so side = √144.
144 = (2 × 2 × 3) × (2 × 2 × 3) = 12 × 12.
So each side is 12 cm.

test.text: Which has no rational square root?

test.ask: A square floor has an area of 2.25 m². Each side = ___ m
test.why:
Side = √2.25.
1.5 × 1.5 = 2.25.
So the side is 1.5 m.

screens.text: Write 100 as a product of prime numbers.
screens.why:
Step 1: 100 = 2 × 50.
Step 2: 50 = 2 × 25.
Step 3: 25 = 5 × 5.
Every factor is now prime: 100 = 2 × 2 × 5 × 5.
10, 50, 4 and 25 are not prime, so the other answers are not finished.
screens.clue: Every factor must be prime. Is 10 prime?
